errors: No outright mathematical errors can be established; the page is enumerative scratch work without stated equalities.
Several lines have alternative or crossed-out entries ('b+Σb+Σa'' after a struck symbol; the struck-out word in the b'^6 a'^2 block). These show Riemann correcting which theta factor survives.
The final block b'^2 a'^6 b^p a^{p-6} is marked uncertain in the transcription. Its superscripts are hard to read, but the pattern (primed sum 8, total 2p+2) fixes them as given.

results.what: Enumeration of distributions of 2p+2 points among the families a, a', b, b' (multiplicity patterns b'^k a'^l b^m a^n), with the theta arguments a+Σa'+Σb etc. arising in each case and identification of the vanishing ones
results.modern_name: Application of the Riemann vanishing theorem (θ(Σ of p−1 points − K)=0) in a residue/interpolation proof of theta-function product identities
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (vanishing theorem, 1857/1865); the general identities of this type: Frobenius, Fay (1973)

results.what: Preparatory casework for multiplicative theta identities of the form Π θ(b'+Σb+Σa^ν−Σb^ν) = Π θ(a'+Σb+Σa^ν−Σb^ν) and a determinant Σ ± Π θ(a+Σa+Σb') on the next page
results.modern_name: Fay-type (trisecant / determinantal) theta identities on Jacobians
results.usually_credited_to: Fay (1973); Frobenius (1880s) for related theta-quotient determinants

deep.surprise_reason: On its own the page is combinatorial bookkeeping of the vanishing of theta arguments, a routine use of Riemann's own vanishing theorem. Its only interest is as preparation for the general theta identities on adjacent folios, which may anticipate Fay-type identities. Nothing on this page itself states such a result.
